Really enjoyed this course and learned a lot, especially in the first system modules even though I have some experience with computers, software, and networks. Glad to see an emphasis on soft skills necessary to deliver high quality support. Soft skills should be mentioned earlier on in the course though and reiterated in Week 6 so people are aware that IT is as much technology as it is people. Would have been nice to see more mentioning of the financial impact that support plays on operations for companies. For example, in the logistics/transportation center, the IT department must ensure that operations has everything they need to generate gross margin. If there is an issue in the companies systems that hinders operations ability to bring in money, the IT department is equally as effected since the IT department doesn't "sell services" rather than provide company upkeep. Rather than provide wikipedia links as "supporting reading documents" these courses should supply in-house made reading documentation that is tailored to the topic and skill level. The majority of wikipedia links dive into "high level" concepts and theorems that are too complex to understand for someone that maybe be entirely new to the IT world. Using wiki links is a bit of an insult and comes off as "just grabs the first link that google search outputs regarding (blank) topic."Furthermore, the placement of some of the popup questions during the video lessons is too "quick." I'm sure that, although difficult and costly, the popup questions should have been included in the video format instead of being placed after-the-fact since it just catches you off guard due to being in between a sentence the instructor hasn't finished.Overall, I am satisfied with the way this course has been developed. Great to have visual aids, transcripts from the video lessons, provided outside coursera/google learning material, and graded assignments/quizzes to ensure user is understanding the material.

I definitely learned some material in this course, but there were gaps as well. Many of the analogies used in explaining technical concepts were unhelpful. I'm thinking especially here of the cookbook analogy in the hardware section. There should be a complete explanation of a concept, followed by an analogy afterward, and the analogy should actually track to the concept. The "limitations of the internet" section was flimsy - the only limitation mentioned was ipv4, with no explanation of the context around ipv4 and ipv6 - not even which one is currently being used. Some of the supplemental readings were helpful, but some (like the links to Windows tech support) were not - I had to independently research some of the topics of the supplemental reading. I don't mind doing independent research, but I would prefer that supplemental reading links at least point to a useful starting point. Finally, it really bothered me that the writing responses in the quizzes were not read or evaluated in any way. I spent time crafting responses to these questions only to realize that gibberish would have worked just as well. I realize that the scale of this course's participation makes reading people's essay responses unfeasible, but I'd prefer that written responses be left off of future quizzes.

I feel that this course was a great introduction to technical support. It gave a somewhat good insight into what a tech support person would face. Sometimes, I wish there was a little more in depth look into the IT world of the topical day of IT. The lessons were good and the discussion forums were good. It lead to some great interaction with others with varies IT experience. Technical support course gave us useful labs to implement on what we had learnt in Course 1. I am not was thrilled working with 3rd party apps to do the lab. I had trouble with the Create a Folder in Windows environment. It took me a way to figure out a solution. Also, I wish that we had a few more lesson that involved the labs. Lastly, I was not able to use the widget for building a computer. I hope that they get it fix  soon. It would help people who do not have a computer to take apart or the tools because they cannot afford the tools. In the end, I gave this course 4 stars. I did not give it 5 stars because I feel there are bugs to work out.  I would suggest that there would be a way to reach out to the instructors besides the class forum to talk with them about an issue with course and get a quicker response.

Love the course! There's some minor gripes I have with the way some things are presented (building the PC in the diagram is a terrible representation of building a PC. I'm just glad that I've actually built many PCs before and knew that it's not that I didn't understand the course material - it's that the diagram has no basis in reality and is completely arbitrary.Aside from that, I've loved the course, the teachers, the writing prompts, everything. It's really well put together and shows a lot of attention to detail.Customer service is something that came natural to me since I started in it at the age of 18, but I notice that not everyone is like me. I was really happy to see the course cover the human aspect of support and how reps must learn to think, act and speak properly so as to not aggravate a situation with a potentially tense customer.

This covered a lot of material and was a good introduction. The video quality and content organization was definitely much better than other online courses I've worked on. That being said, the labs were glitchy and some of the evaluations were so basic that I didn't feel like they were actually doing much of anything to test my understanding. I would also recommend adding examples for the peer graded assignment--the responses were all over the place and it's difficult to give an evaluation when there's nothing to use as a baseline. I'm a little over halfway through the second course in the specialization now and while it's a steep learning curve between the two, I'm enjoying the networking course quite a bit more because I feel more challenged by the content than the interface while I'm doing the evaluations.

I learned so much over the last 6 weeks. I recommend that the certification description include information about building a computer. If you want the students to really do this they need to have this information upfront. Please consider offering a package with the components and any interested student has the option of doing this exercise. I believe a breakout group could be created for the students who want to complete this exercise. It connects them as a team and offers them the opportunity to share their information and experience with future students. I have other thoughts on making this type of exercise a robust experience. I look forward to the course module on networking. Thanks You

Overall I think this course is amazing. Speaking as someone who has finished a associates degree in computer information systems, I feel like this course does a better job of teaching the same IT knowledge at a fraction of the cost. The only real downside is the lack of extra classes like oral communication and whatever other electives you would normally mix in. I would have given it 5 stars but I ran into some major technical issues with qwiklabs not connected as well as not properly grading assignments but after waiting a few days everything started functioning properly again.

There was some interesting content, and it took things from the ground up. They tried hard to give a personal touch and make a learning community, and give it a personal touch.Coming from intermediate-level experience, I found it frustratingly slow paced, but it states up front that it is a beginner level course. I suppose that that is being rather impatient as I finished it in less than 24 hours. I have high hopes for this sequence. I think that it is well made, and I think that I will really enjoy later courses as it ventures into territory that is more novel to me.

Well put together course.  Does what it is intended to do.  Instructors are professional. I think it would be very useful to have a rewind 5 or 10 second button for the videos.  Additionally, for some learners, such as myself, it is easier to have a more reading friendly format for the courses.  The transcript is good, but if you only read it and don't watch the videos, you can miss out on some key pictures and diagrams that really clarify the material.  Solution I see to this is perhaps having slides or inputting the pictures into the transcript.  Overall, fantastic.

I would always have two options for Peer graded assignments, especially if the last assignment for the course is peer graded as I would have loved to continue on in the course while waiting for it to be graded. two ways this could have been done, one is to allow for continuation of the course while waiting for the peer graded assignment (I think you allow for this but it isn't easily shown), the other one is to allow another option that doesn't require waiting for peers to do it. overall though, great first course, enjoyed reviewing the fundamentals/basics

The course is interesting and informative, but in some areas lacked in depth instructions that left the user guessing on what to do and how to do it.  For a novice user or even someone that's had some use with computers this wouldn't be a problem. This certificate, however, says it is for all people, even those with absolutely no experience with computers. With that in mind, I believe every assignment should clearly be marked with a how to, so even first time users know what they are doing. Very good course so far though and I like it a lot.

I think it was a good course overall, I already knew most of the lessons that were taught. Even though I knew most of the lessons before hand I still found these lessons as great refreshers here and there. I also learned some new stuff along the way. The only complaint that I would have is the, instructors or teachers of this course felt very scripted in the way they talked. At some points it got hard to listen to them because the teachers had no emotion it seemed like. Either than that the content was good in this course.

Overall good.  The videos could be improved by using less of a pure face-to-face lecture format, and taking advantage of more graphic displays and animations to help the student visualize things.  In addition, it would be helpful to slow down through some of the more technical sections, and provide a better context for what the various acronyms mean, and to explain in a little more detail what’s going on.  The additional context provides the learner a better way to assimilate the new information in a more useful way.

Some icons look very similar and can be confusing, for example the Preview and Submit icon for submitting the final Effective Documentation paper, the PBJ sheet. I found it very confusing when the image seems to be the very same one I was just looking at. I would suggest at least change the color of the next icon to something besides the very same blue. I kinda figure some of this may be intentional to help weed out those just playing with the course versus those very serious about learning more than they began with.

I love this course. It makes everything easy to understand. The only thing that could be better in my opionon, is the coursera / qwiklab integration. No matter how many times I did my labs and followed ALL the steps and the instructions on how to get a grade posted to coursera (including hitting the red end lab button), The grade would not post. I had to contact support to get both labs to post a grade for me. That was resolved very quickly though!! Overall, these courses are awesome for newbies to tech :)

This is a good introductory course to IT. I really enjoyed it. Some of the lessons are presented in a wordy manner. I wish they would focus on what you need to know versus all the extra stuff. There was so much much " but we will learn that later on". The Peer review can be frustrating as there is no instructor. You have to rely that that peer is understanding the information and accurately grading you. If they do not understand the material and give you a bad review, you risk failing the course.

I feel that the quizzes were a bit bare-bones. Also the question interruptions were far too easy to warrant interruption. They would usually say that a certain noun and within seconds of hearing the description of the noun they'd give you the description and ask for the noun. It was somewhat distracting, but maybe it helped me remember it.Other than that this is definitely a good course for beginners. It outlines all of the basics of computing and its interaction with the outside world.

I wish the quizzes were longer with more questions so that I could better gauge how well I'm learning and retaining all the information. I also wish the assignments were a bit more involved. However, I know we're just learning the very basics right now, and am hoping that the following course assignments will be more in-depth. Overall, I think the information is being presented in a way that makes it very easy to understand for even the most novice of computer users. Thank you!

Great Introduction course, but I felt that the section where we learn to build a PC should've been more concise in instructions and other helpful tools/tips when building your own PC. Although part of this course is of course extra curricular and you can access additional tools and information online, I thought it would've been helpful. Also to make the discussion pages more of a mandatory thing, I think it could potentially help students engage and socialize with each others.

I think this course is great for beginners and people that have been in the IT industry. For the beginners it teaches the basic fundamentals. For the people that have been in the IT industry doing a refresher and the section on Customer Service is a great tool to learn the skills. The course is well laid out and easy to understand, There are some areas that need improvement as in grading other work and submitting feed back. Feedback area was hard to see in the Chrome browser.

Great beginner material. I feel that some of the mistakes that were made during the video need to be re-shot though instead of adding an addendum on the top of the video. Especially for someone new to the field, first impressions can be vital and it's important not to give incorrect information, even if you are correcting it right away. The human subconscious is powerful so you don't want information being repeated to impressionable new IT support students.

Overall, a very good course. I gave it a 4 rather than a 5 due to some glitches with the labs on the topic of installation/update/removal of applications.Most videos are 5 minutes or less (which is appropriate for the attention span of your average person).It is helpful to have the transcript of each video as well as access to subtitles.It would be helpful to have more frequent quizzes or knowledge checks within the videos.

I loved it when something basic was being covered that showed me a gap in my knowledge that i could then read up on and also got assured that it would be covered in more detail in a future module.

I liked the instructors and the way the materials were presented.  I also liked being able to discuss materials in the forums.  I think we were the very first class for this, so i am not surprised some things weren't completely functioning 100%. I think it was good for beginners. I have been working in IT for some years now and wanted to take this course as I am trying to work at Google in the near future. aside from some caching issue when unintalling/installing softwares where the UID/PW will not validate. Entire course went smoothly. I know it was fundamentals but wish it was a little more in depth.  A lot of mentioning stuff and saying we will talk about that later on in the course.  Don't get me wrong it was a great refresher, but It would have gotten 5 stars if not for the brevity of information.
